criteria.criterion: athena-data defines athena.host-error/1 with status_code (optional integer), operation (closed list including merge, create-pr, read-repo), job, phase, at, and a closed message_class; the raw stderr text is not a stored field.
criteria.evidence: records.rs defines `HostError` with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` and the fields id, at, status_code: Option<u16>, operation, job, phase and message_class. `HostOperation` is the closed list merge, create-pr, read-repo, read-pr and read-checks. `MessageClass` is a closed 8-value enum derived from the status, and the gate refuses a record whose class does not match its status. There is no text field. Tests check that a record carrying stderr is refused, and that no gh text reaches the JSON.

criteria.criterion: athena-data defines append-only athena.decision-state/1 (decision id, state, firing record ids, date) with a fold to current state, and athena.default-expectations/1 (default_id, assumptions, signals, defaults version, proposal).
criteria.evidence: `DecisionState` has id, at, decision, state (under-review or cleared), signal, firing_records and decision_job. `fold_decision_states` keeps the latest state per decision, ordered by (at, id). `DefaultExpectations` has default_id, assumptions, signals, defaults_version and proposal, plus validation. Both types are added to `AnyRecord` with paths under records/.

criteria.criterion: The gh client extracts the HTTP status from a refused call, writes a host-error record, and retries a 5xx a bounded number of times before returning the error; non-5xx errors are not retried.
criteria.evidence: gh.rs: `GhCli` returns a `GhFailure` carrying `parse_status(stderr)`. `GhClient::api` logs every refusal to the `HostErrorLog` and repeats the call only when `is_transient` (500, 502, 503 or 504), up to `retry.attempts` (3 by default) with an injectable delay. Any other failure is returned at once. 501 counts as non-transient, which matches the accepted reading.

criteria.criterion: The land path invokes the watcher after a host error and at landing; the watcher loads D87's hard signal (operation merge, status 405 or 422, one job), validates values against the vocabulary, and does not evaluate records from a firing's own introspection.
criteria.evidence: The `land --pr` code in gh.rs captures the landing outcome, then calls `self.watch_landing(&log, ui)` before returning it, so the watcher also runs after a failed landing. watcher.rs: `D87_SIGNAL` is checked by `load()` against the operation, phase and status vocabulary, and a hard signal's threshold is fixed at 1. `evaluate` reads only host-error and decision-state records, skips host errors a state record already cites, and skips a decision already under review. The landing logic lives in gh.rs, not land.rs, pr.rs or run.rs, which is acceptable.

summary: The change does what the request asks, and I recommend it pass. The GitHub client (`GhCli`) now reads the HTTP status from gh's "(HTTP nnn)" text. Every refused call goes into a typed athena.host-error/1 record that does not store gh's own error text. A 500, 502, 503 or 504 is tried up to 3 times in total, and only the last failure reaches the user. Retry and recording happen in `GhClient::api`, so they cover the read-repo call that failed for job w4cj, not just the merge. Every run of `athena land --pr` ends by running the watcher, whether the landing succeeded or failed. The watcher commits the run's host-error records and checks them against D87's hard signal (merge refused with 405 or 422, one job), which is validated against the record vocabulary. When the signal fires, it appends one athena.decision-state/1 record, so D87 goes under review on the first occurrence. The athena.default-expectations/1 record type has a writer and a reader. `athena backtest` reads records/host-errors/ and reports D87 under review, citing the record id. The brief component and set selection are held back as the request allowed, and the design doc, docs/records.md and CHANGELOG.md all describe the change. I ran the relevant tests, clippy and fmt, and all passed. There are two minor findings: two test files are outside the deliverables list, and no single test runs the full `land --pr` path through to the decision-state record.
